{"id": "a0d909b0-c1f3-452c-97cb-acc117b617c4", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "I looked into this and didn't find a feature specifically called "sustainability review" in AWS DevOps Agent's documented capabilities — it's not one of the review types I have (Release Readiness Review, Release Testing, QA Testing, Investigations, Recommendations). If you're referring to something else — maybe a Well-Architected sustainability-pillar check, or a custom agent/skill someone set up in your space — let me know and I can look that up specifically.

That said, I can tell you how my AWS access works in general, since the same guardrails apply no matter what kind of review or analysis runs:

- **Any read-only calls** (describe/list/get operations — the bulk of what a sustainability-style audit would use: resource inventories, utilization metrics, idle resource checks, tagging, etc.) run autonomously with no approval needed and change nothing.
- **Any mutating call** (create/update/modify) requires per-action operator approval before it executes — nothing fires silently.
- **Permanently blocked, never attempted, regardless of approval:**
  - Delete or remove any AWS resource
  - Change permissions, policies, or access controls (IAM, resource policies, public-access settings, org policies, and similar) — except security group ingress rule changes, which are allowed with approval (egress changes and security group deletion remain blocked)

So if what you're picturing is an audit-style pass over your production account (checking for idle/oversized/unused resources, right-sizing opportunities, etc.), it would only read data by default — it would never delete resources or touch IAM/policies, and any actual remediation step would show up as an explicit approval request rather than running on its own.

If you'd like, I can check whether there's an actual sustainability-focused skill or custom agent configured in your space.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
